findings.title: Returned SQL fragments contain top-level OR without enclosing parentheses
findings.body: `getBaseConditions()` returns the authorization fragment verbatim when no filters are set (line 75), and for `org`/`team` scope that fragment is built by the reduce as `(A AND "isTeamBooking" = true) OR (B AND "isTeamBooking" = false)` with no enclosing parentheses (lines 171-174 and 204-207). The same is true for `getFilterConditions()` when only `eventTypeId` is set (`("eventTypeId" = x) OR ("eventParentId" = x)`). Because `AND` binds tighter than `OR` in SQL, any consumer that composes the fragment with extra predicates — e.g. `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "startTime" >= ${from}` — produces `A OR (B AND startTime >= ...)`, so the additional predicate constrains only one branch of the OR. The result is silently widened row sets, i.e. a potential authorization/scope bypass and wrong insights numbers. The fragments should be wrapped (`Prisma.sql`(${cond})`) before being returned. Note the only test uses `WHERE ${baseConditions}` standalone, so this failure mode is not covered.

findings.title: Public findMany() removed without updating any callers
findings.body: The public method `findMany(findManyArgs: Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs)`, which ran `prisma.bookingTimeStatusDenormalized.findMany` with the authorization and filter where-clauses applied, is deleted and replaced by `getBaseConditions()` returning a raw `Prisma.Sql`. No other file in the repository is touched by this PR, so any existing consumer of `InsightsBookingService.findMany` will no longer compile, and consumers must now hand-write raw SQL (taking on responsibility for parenthesization, column quoting and result typing). Either keep a `findMany`-style convenience wrapper or update the call sites in this PR. The PR description also states that only the tests changed and that the service was already converted, which hides this breaking change from reviewers.

findings.title: New InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions weakens compile-time validation of options
findings.body: The constructor parameter type changed from the zod discriminated union (`InsightsBookingServiceOptions`, which requires `teamId` when `scope === "team"`) to the hand-written `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` with `scope: "user" | "org" | "team"` and optional `teamId`. A caller can now pass `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` without `teamId` and it type-checks; at runtime `safeParse` fails, `this.options` becomes `null`, and the service silently returns `1=0`, i.e. an empty result set with no error or log. The previous typing made this a compile error. Keep the discriminated union as the constructor type (or at least log/throw when validation fails) so misuse is caught instead of producing silently empty insights.

findings.title: Unreachable branches in getBaseConditions
findings.body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` always resolves to a `Prisma.Sql` object (at minimum `NOTHING_CONDITION`), and objects are always truthy, so the `else if (filterConditions)` branch (line 76) and the final `else return NOTHING_CONDITION` (line 79) can never execute. The dead code suggests the author expected auth conditions to possibly be null/absent; if a future change makes auth conditions optional the fallback would silently drop authorization. Either drop the dead branches or make the nullability explicit.

findings.title: Caching tests deleted although the caching logic still exists
findings.body: The `describe("Caching")` block (previously asserting that `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` return the same cached value on repeated calls) was removed, but the service still implements `cachedAuthConditions` / `cachedFilterConditions` memoization, including the `undefined`-vs-`null` distinction in `getFilterConditions()` (a cached `null` must not trigger a rebuild). That memoization path is now untested, so a regression such as caching `null` incorrectly or rebuilding conditions on every call would go unnoticed. The tests could simply be ported to the new `Prisma.sql` expectations instead of deleted.

findings.title: Org/team scope assertions depend on unspecified DB row ordering
findings.body: The org-scope expectation hard-codes the parameter arrays as `[org.id, team.id, team2.id, team3.id]` and `[user.id, user2.id, user3.id]`. These come from `TeamRepository.findAllByParentId` and `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds`, which issue queries without an `ORDER BY`, so PostgreSQL does not guarantee the returned order. With `toEqual` on the `Prisma.Sql` object the `values` arrays are compared element-by-element, so any reordering (e.g. after a vacuum, index-only scan or parallel plan) fails the test even though the generated SQL is semantically equivalent. Sort the ids in the service (or sort before comparison in the test) to make the assertion deterministic.
